slowest_experiments.label: Exp 53: Runtime constraint instrumentation
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: Cold-start infrastructure experiment requiring constraint framework construction from scratch. This experiment now appears as the top outlier in FIVE consecutive milestone retros (2026.04.17 through 2026.04.21). Root cause has never been addressed — the fix (milestone cold-start scaffolding template reusing prior experiment infrastructure) has been recommended in four consecutive retros and implemented in zero. Exp 53 alone consumes 9.8% of the total milestone wall time.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 219: Live GSM8K semantic benchmark on Qwen3.5-0.8B and Gemma
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: Sequential model loading — Qwen then Gemma evaluated on a single GPU in sequence. DualGPURunner was available from Exp 258 (prior milestone) and became the default for new GPU experiments this milestone (Exps 282/283), but Exp 219 predates that and was not re-run. No inference batching; each of the 200 GSM8K cases was a single forward pass. Second RTX 3090 idle throughout this experiment.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 184: 3B model verification — does verify-repair help large models
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: 3B-parameter model requires significantly more VRAM and per-call latency than the 0.8B baseline. Verify-repair loop multiplied forward passes (baseline → verify → repair → re-verify) on a single GPU with no batching or parallelization. Second GPU idle throughout. Not re-run with DualGPURunner.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 221: Live prompt-side constraint benchmark on typed IR tasks
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: Typed IR generation pipeline ran sequentially across prompt variants with single-threaded constraint evaluation. DualGPUBenchmarkHarness (Exp 258) was available this milestone but Exp 221 was not re-run or replaced with a parallelized version.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 155: Retrain JEPA violation predictor v2 with multi-domain data
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: Multi-domain retraining required full dataset reload and feature extraction per domain in sequence on CPU (JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu). Correct for reproducibility, but the large corpus would benefit from batched CPU parallelism (multiprocessing per domain). No GPU training pipeline invoked.

carry_over_note: All 5 slowest experiments are IDENTICAL to those flagged in the 2026.04.18, 2026.04.19, and 2026.04.20 retros. This is the 5th consecutive milestone with the same top outlier (Exp 53 at 418 min). Despite carry-over rate dropping from 100% on action items in the 2026.04.21 session (DualGPURunner and checkpointing resolved for new experiments), the historical slow experiments from early in the research program (Exps 53, 155, 184, 219, 221) have never been revisited or re-run with the improved infrastructure.

action_item_audit.description: Wire DualGPURunner from Exp 281 — DualGPUBenchmarkHarness as the default scheduler for experiments that reference two or more models.
action_item_audit.evidence: Exps 282 and 283 explicitly wired DualGPURunner at construction time. DualGPURunner active from the first GPU-using experiment in the milestone window.

action_item_audit.description: Add per-question checkpointing to all live GSM8K, HumanEval, and constraint_ir loops — checkpoint every 10 questions.
action_item_audit.evidence: Exps 282 and 283 implemented per-question checkpointing at 10-question intervals with 60s hard timeout per inference call. Worst-case restart cost bounded to 10 questions.

action_item_audit.description: Complete the Apple adversarial benchmark end-to-end: generate dataset, run GPU baseline, run verify-repair, produce conclusive classification in Exp 284.
action_item_audit.evidence: Exp 284 returned INCONCLUSIVE: Exps 282 and 283 produced partial artifacts (stall_at set) due to live GPU unavailability. Dataset exists (Exp 281, 400 rows) and infrastructure exists, but live result data is absent. Carried to PROCESS-001.

action_item_audit.description: Standardize CPU ORT + GPU LLM hybrid: CPU ORT for linear gate at batch_size < 32, GPU LLM for language model calls, test CUDA ORT at batch_size >= 32.
action_item_audit.evidence: No experiment in the 281-293 range tested CUDA ORT at batch_size >= 32. The CPU-ORT/CUDA-ORT crossover remains unvalidated for a second consecutive milestone. Carried to PROCESS-002.

structural_improvements_this_milestone.note: Two of four action items from the prior retro were resolved. This breaks the 100% carry-over streak for action items (new experiments). However, the historical slow experiments (Exps 53, 155, 184, 219, 221) remain unchanged — they account for 774 minutes (18.2% of total wall time) and have never been re-run with improved infrastructure.

gpu_utilization_analysis.sequential_vs_parallel_assessment: Both GPUs idle at milestone end — fifth consecutive milestone with this pattern. The 2MB residual on each GPU indicates no cleanup hook has been added despite four retro recommendations. GPU utilization during the milestone is unknown because gpu_monitor.py was not run in continuous --loop mode. The DualGPURunner was wired for Exps 282/283 but those experiments stalled due to live GPU unavailability. The ~774 minutes of wall time in the top-5 slowest experiments all predate DualGPURunner and ran with one GPU only.
gpu_utilization_analysis.peak_utilization_observed: Unknown — gpu_monitor.py not run in continuous mode for the 5th consecutive milestone
gpu_utilization_analysis.residual_vram_pattern: 2MB on each GPU at milestone end — identical to 2026.04.19 and 2026.04.20. gpu_monitor --kill-zombies teardown hook still not added.

experiments_that_could_have_been_paralle: Exp 282 (Apple baseline GPU) and Exp 283 (Apple verify-repair) — sequential runs on the same corpus. Could have been dispatched to GPU 0 and GPU 1 concurrently with a shared dataset reader.
Exp 289 (FpgaBackend implementation) and Exp 291 (JEPA Apple retrain) — independent experiments with no data dependency. Could have been parallelized on separate cores or staged concurrently.
Exp 292 (AMD XDNA NPU benchmark) and Exp 293 (HuggingFace publish) — entirely independent; both ran on CPU. Could have been parallelized in separate processes.
parallelization_analysis.note: This milestone had fewer GPU experiments than prior milestones (most experiments targeted FPGA, NPU, HF publishing, or CPU-only pipelines). The parallelism gain is lower than prior milestones. However, the conductor still dispatches experiments sequentially by default — no experiment-level parallelism planner exists.

preflight_test_suite_analysis.note: Doc-only provenance sync passes continue to trigger full test suite runs. The doc-only test classifier (run only test_docs.py for docs-only diffs) was recommended in four consecutive retros and not implemented. Each avoidable full-suite run adds ~45s; the three avoidable runs this milestone cost ~2.25 minutes — small in absolute terms but indicative of the pattern persisting.

doc_reconciliation_analysis.note: Two doc reconciliation passes observed: Exp 293 README update and ops/status.md/changelog.md updates. Both triggered at least partial suite validation. The provenance auto-sync hook (counts result JSONs and updates README/docs automatically) was recommended in four consecutive retros and not implemented.

bottlenecks_identified: SYSTEMIC: Top-5 slowest experiments unchanged for the 5th consecutive milestone (Exps 53, 219, 184, 221, 155). These predate DualGPURunner and have never been re-run. Together they consume 774 minutes (18.2% of total wall time). The research program has grown around them rather than fixing them.

Exp 53 cold-start outlier: 418 minutes (9.8% of milestone). Five retros have recommended a scaffolding template to eliminate this. No template has been created. This single experiment costs more than 30 average experiments.

GPU under-utilization persists: both RTX 3090s idle at milestone end, 2MB residual, 0% utilization. Peak utilization unknown for the 5th consecutive milestone (no continuous gpu_monitor). Live GPU inference experiments (282/283) stalled — effective GPU utilization on new experiments may be near zero.

Apple adversarial benchmark still INCONCLUSIVE: Exps 282/283 produced partial artifacts due to live GPU unavailability. The benchmark has been deferred for two milestones. The stall mechanism (60s timeout per inference call) is correct but the underlying cause — live GPU access blocked in the conductor environment — has not been diagnosed.

CUDA ORT batch_size >= 32 crossover point still untested: the CPU ORT vs CUDA ORT comparison from Exp 259 has not been followed up in two consecutive milestones. The optimal batch routing strategy remains unvalidated.

Sequential dispatch in the conductor: all 13 experiments this milestone ran sequentially. At least 3 pairs had no data dependency and could have been parallelized. The conductor has no dependency-graph-based parallel dispatch capability.
gpu_monitor.py not running continuously: peak GPU utilization is unknown for the 5th consecutive milestone. The --loop monitoring recommendation has appeared in every retro since 2026.04.18.

gpu_monitor --kill-zombies not added to conductor teardown: 2MB residual VRAM on each GPU at milestone end for 5th consecutive milestone. Minor in size but the pattern indicates no cleanup automation has been added.
Provenance auto-sync not implemented: manual README/docs updates for artifact counts continue to trigger doc-sync passes and occasional full suite runs.

Short milestone window effect: Exps 281-293 represent only the final session of the full 312-experiment milestone. The bulk of the 4261-minute wall time came from prior sessions that accumulated the Exp 53-class bottlenecks. The conductor has no cross-session throughput regression detector.
improvements_suggested: CRITICAL: Create a milestone cold-start scaffolding template that pre-wires DualGPUBenchmarkHarness, per-question checkpointing at 10q intervals, CPU ORT gate, and standard artifact schema. The FIRST experiment of every milestone should be 'validate scaffold', not 'build infrastructure' — this eliminates the Exp-53-class outlier pattern entirely. Expected saving: ~390 min/milestone (9%).

CRITICAL: Re-run Exps 53, 219, 184, 221, and 155 with the current infrastructure (DualGPURunner, per-question checkpointing, inference batching at batch_size=8). These five experiments contribute 774 minutes (18.2%) of milestone wall time each milestone they are not fixed. Even a 50% reduction would save ~387 min/milestone.

Diagnose live GPU unavailability root cause: Exps 282 and 283 stalled (stall_at set) despite DualGPURunner being wired at construction. The Apple adversarial benchmark is in its third milestone of INCONCLUSIVE status. Determine whether the issue is VRAM exhaustion, CUDA context conflict, CARNOT_SKIP_LLM=1 in CI, or conductor environment isolation — and fix it.

Add a doc-only test classifier to the conductor: if git diff --name-only touches only README.md, docs/, ops/, results/*.json, _bmad/traceability.md — run only tests/python/test_docs.py (5 tests, ~1s) instead of the full 3500-test suite. Saves 2-4 avoidable full-suite runs per milestone.
Add a provenance auto-sync pre-commit hook: count results/experiment_*_results.json and write the count into README.md and docs/index.html before every commit. Zero manual sync passes required.

Add gpu_monitor.py --kill-zombies to conductor teardown after each experiment. Add gpu_monitor.py --loop --interval 60 as a background daemon from conductor start, writing to results/gpu_utilization_YYYYMMDD.jsonl. The 5th retro recommendation for this — add it as a tracked PROCESS ticket.

Add a parallelism planner to the conductor: parse experiment data-dependency graph and dispatch independent experiments concurrently. Even 2-slot parallel dispatch reduces wall time on independent pairs (Exps 292+293 this milestone would have been free parallelism).

Validate CUDA ORT batch_size >= 32 crossover: run one focused experiment (Exp 295 candidate) measuring CPU ORT vs CUDA ORT at batch_size 1, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64. Standardize the routing decision. This is the third milestone this is deferred.

Add a throughput regression alarm to the conductor: track experiments_per_hour across milestones in ops/metrics.md and emit a WARNING if rate drops more than 5% from the prior milestone. Rate has been flat at 4.2-4.4 exp/hour for four milestones — a regression alarm would surface stagnation earlier.

Convert all remaining deferred action items (PROCESS-001, PROCESS-002) to prioritized stories with explicit pre-milestone acceptance criteria and a milestone-block rule: do not start the next milestone without resolving these tickets.
